objective: Add a small read-only `orc tui` terminal interface using Ratatui and Crossterm, reusing Orc application/domain APIs without introducing lifecycle or persistence semantics.
assumptions: The root Rust crate owns the `orc` CLI; existing task/query APIs are discoverable from the application/domain/storage modules.
The implementation may add a minimal read-only application API only if no suitable existing task-queue query exists.
Automated review will execute the required validation commands after implementation.
risks: Terminal restoration must remain reliable across normal exits and managed error paths.
The TUI must preserve existing task ordering and lifecycle terminology while avoiding TUI-specific SQL or state transitions.
The event loop must remain thin and keep navigation state testable independently of a real terminal.

tasks.title: Expose the read-only task queue
tasks.objective: Provide the TUI with an authoritative read-only task queue through existing Orc APIs.
expected_changes: Reuse the existing task-list/query API or add the smallest provider-independent read-only application method.
Add a stable TUI-facing task row/read-model conversion while preserving existing ordering and terminology.
Add focused behavioral tests for populated and empty queues and assigned-agent availability.
unchanged: Lifecycle transitions and task mutation behavior.
Raw SQL outside the storage layer.
acceptance_criteria: A read-only task-queue query is available through the existing Orc application/domain boundary.
Returned data preserves existing task ordering and exposes task ID, title, status, priority, and assigned agent when available.
No TUI-specific SQL or lifecycle mutation path is introduced.
The API handles empty queues without error or fabricated records.
required_tests: Query a populated queue through the production application boundary and verify all required display fields.
Query an empty queue and verify a successful empty result.
Verify task ordering matches the existing queue semantics.

execution_hints.effort_reason: Requires tracing the existing application and storage boundaries and proving read-model data flow without persistence changes.

tasks.title: Build the TUI state and rendering core
tasks.objective: Implement the terminal-independent TUI state, navigation, and read-only task queue rendering.
expected_changes: Add Ratatui and Crossterm dependencies at versions compatible with the existing Rust project.
Add modular TUI state, task-row/view-model, input-action, and rendering components.
Implement bounded Up/Down selection and quit action handling without domain mutations.
Add terminal-independent tests for rendering data mapping, navigation bounds, quit inputs, and empty queues.
unchanged: Task mutations, lifecycle actions, refresh, logs, and detail panes.
acceptance_criteria: TUI application state is independent of terminal I/O and event backend code.
Rows render ID, title, status, priority, and assigned agent when available.
Up and Down update selection within bounds without mutating task data or Orc state.
Empty queues render cleanly and have no invalid selection.
`q` and `Esc` are represented as quit actions in the terminal-independent input/state layer.
required_tests: Verify Up and Down navigation at the first, middle, and last selectable rows.
Verify navigation over an empty queue does not panic or create a selection.
Verify q and Esc produce quit actions.
Verify every required task field is mapped to the rendered row representation.

execution_hints.effort_reason: The state and rendering split is localized but requires careful input semantics, bounds handling, empty-state behavior, and testable presentation mapping.

tasks.title: Wire `orc tui` and safe terminal lifecycle
tasks.objective: Integrate the TUI core into the `orc tui` command with safe Crossterm terminal lifecycle management.
tasks.role: Integrate the CLI command and terminal runtime
expected_changes: Add the `tui` CLI command to the existing command routing layer.
Implement a managed terminal session/guard that restores raw mode and alternate-screen state on normal and recoverable error paths.
Connect task loading, event polling, input handling, rendering, and quit behavior using the TUI core.
Add focused integration or seam tests proving terminal cleanup sequencing and CLI command dispatch without mutating Orc state.
unchanged: Lifecycle state machine, scheduler, provider, quota, validation, review, blocker, and persistence semantics.
Dispatch, review, revise, accept, requeue, unblock, reject, cancel, refresh, and orchestration controls.
acceptance_criteria: `orc tui` starts the Ratatui/Crossterm interface and loads the current task queue through the read-only application API.
Terminal initialization enables raw mode and alternate-screen handling through a managed execution path.
Normal exit via q or Esc restores terminal state.
Recoverable errors from the managed TUI path restore terminal state before returning the error.
The event loop delegates navigation and rendering to the terminal-independent TUI core and performs no lifecycle or task mutations.
required_tests: Invoke the CLI routing path for `orc tui` and verify it reaches the TUI runtime.
Exercise normal quit and verify terminal restoration is requested.
Inject a recoverable runtime error and verify restoration occurs before the error is returned.
Verify the runtime uses the read-only task API and performs no task or lifecycle mutations.

execution_hints.effort_reason: Terminal setup, restoration, and managed error cleanup form a lifecycle-sensitive integration boundary with interactive event handling and CLI wiring.
